title: Qualify and Route Demo Requests in Seconds
summary: Answer every demo request while the visitor is still on the page: identify the company from the work email, check it against your ICP, land the account and contact, tell the team in Slack, and show a booking link or a thank-you. How Cargo's inbound-qualification cookbook does it with a public form on a Cargo tool, what each submission costs, and what it will not do.
body_markdown:
**To qualify and route demo requests in seconds, make the demo form itself the qualification step: each submission identifies the company from the work email’s domain, checks it against your ICP rules, lands the account and the contact, posts once to your sales channel, and answers on the page with your booking link if they fit and a thank-you if they do not.** There is no queue for a lead to cool in, nights and weekends included, because no person sits between the submit button and the answer.


The[inbound-qualification cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/inbound-qualification) declares this as one Cargo tool with a public form, so there is no backend to run and no form vendor. This page covers the path a submission takes, what it costs, and where it stops.


## Deploy it#


The form sits on a site hosted on Cargo, usually from[build and host your company website](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/build-and-host-your-company-website-on-your-own-domain) . Inside that project:


shellscript


```text
npm   install   -g   @cargo-ai/cli
cargo-ai   login   --email   you@company.com


cargo-ai   project   add   cookbook/inbound-qualification
npm   install   @cargo-ai/form-sdk   --prefix   infra/website-building/apps/website
cargo-ai   project   plan
cargo-ai   project   deploy


```


Four values are yours to set before the deploy: the ICP rules (` icpMinEmployees` ,` icpMaxEmployees` ,` icpCountries` ), the` bookingUrl` , the Slack channel id, and` publicForm.allowedOrigins` , your site’s canonical origin exactly, with no trailing slash. The website app receives the tool’s uuid as` NEXT_PUBLIC_CARGO_FORM` .


## How a submission is handled#


text


```text
visitor submits /contact/ (headless @cargo-ai/form-sdk, your own markup)
-> public form API: origin, honeypot, time-trap, rate limit
-> tool inbound_form:
personal email domain?   -> "work_email_required", nothing paid, nothing written
LinkedIn enrichCompanyFromDomain on the email domain
ICP rules: employee_count within the band, hq_country in the list
upsert gtm_accounts (matched on website) and gtm_contacts (matched on email)
one Slack post to the locked channel
<- "qualified" + booking link, or "not_qualified"


```


**Checked in order, each one refusing the request:** an origin not in` allowedOrigins` gets a 403; a filled honeypot field is dropped; a submission sooner than` minFillMillis` (3,000 ms in the example) after the SDK loaded is refused; more than ten submissions a minute from one address are rate-limited; a CAPTCHA (Turnstile or hCaptcha) applies only if you add it; and the workflow refuses a personal email before any paid call.


**The page waits up to 30 seconds.** The form submits in async mode and the SDK polls the run, with` pollTimeoutMs: 30_000` . A run is mostly the company lookup. If it runs past the timeout the visitor gets the thank-you, and the run still finishes: the account, the contact and the Slack post land late, never lost.


**Rules, not a model call, on the submission path.** A headcount band and a list of ISO country codes are free, explainable and give the same answer twice. Swapping them for an agent that reads your ICP is the` agent-qualification` variation, at the price of a model call per submission and a less predictable answer.


Cargo platform data, 90 days to Oct 16 2026: company enrichment, the job the form runs on every work email, returned a company in 91.6% of 2.45 million runs across 210 workspaces. A domain with no company match is written and posted as` unknown_company` , without a qualification.


## What lands where#


Where What


` gtm_accounts`` website` (the email domain),` name` ,` number_of_employees` ,` billing_country` ,` linkedin_url` ,` description`


` gtm_contacts`` email` ,` first_name` ,` last_name` ,` name` ,` account_id` ,` lead_source`` website` , plus` inbound_status` ,` inbound_message` ,` inbound_page_url` ,` utm_source` ,` utm_campaign` ,` marketing_consent`


Slack one message: who, which company and domain, headcount and country, the message they wrote, the page


The page the booking link, or the thank-you


A second submission from the same person updates their row instead of adding one.


**Deep research, after the answer.** A separate play,` research_qualified_leads` , ships disabled. Once enabled it runs every 15 minutes for contacts marked` qualified` and not yet researched: an agent reads your ICP and tiering rubric from the workspace context, uses at most four web searches, and writes` inbound_tier` (A, B, C or disqualified),` inbound_brief` ,` inbound_rationale` and` inbound_researched_at` onto the contact, with a short note to the same channel. It never runs inside the form, so the visitor never waits on it.


## Routing beyond one channel#


As shipped, routing is the booking link for a fit and one locked Slack channel for the team. Two variations take it further:` owner-routing` assigns` owner_id` by territory or round robin before the post and mentions the owner, and` crm-backed` writes to HubSpot, Salesforce or Attio instead of the shared models. For territory, round-robin and capacity rules as a product feature, see[routing](https://www.getcargo.ai/features/routing) , and for why assignment often moves out of the CRM,[alternatives to CRM-native lead routing](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/alternatives-to-crm-native-lead-routing) .


## What it costs#


Step Credits (list price)


A work-email submission (LinkedIn` enrichCompanyFromDomain` ) 0.5


A personal-email submission 0


The research play, per qualified contact, once enabled LLM tokens plus up to four web searches


Read the live price with` cargo-ai connection integration get linkedin` . The tool also bills orchestration steps (1 credit per 100) and the models storage upserts (1 credit per 1,000). The origin allow-list keeps other sites from spending your credits.


## What it will not do#


- **Enrich the person.** The company is looked up from the domain; no person lookup, personal email or phone search runs on a submitter.
- **Accept a personal email** unless you choose the` accept-personal-email` variation, which leaves those contacts without an account.
- **Book the meeting.**` qualified` means the company fits and was shown the link; whether they booked lives in your scheduling tool.
- **Send marketing email** without the consent box ticked. A demo request alone is not consent to a newsletter.
- **Set a cookie before a submit.** The SDK sets its` cargo_anon_id` cookie only when a visitor submits, and not under Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track.


Deploy it from the[inbound-qualification cookbook](https://www.getcargo.ai/cookbooks/inbound-qualification) . To score a list rather than a form, see[how to qualify a list of leads against your ICP](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/automated-lead-qualification) ; to add the companies that read the site without filling anything in,[turn website visitors into routed, qualified leads](https://www.getcargo.ai/blog/turn-website-visitors-into-routed-qualified-leads) .
